Accounts can also be given the judge role. It currently has no screens of its own beyond the public ones; see the Judge page.

Accounts are created by the event administrator. See Users and passwords.

docs.title: I am a screen and AV operator
docs.text:
You put TMS on the venue's screens and speakers. There are two public screens, and neither needs a login.

Your screens

Scoreboard and Timer, both on the home screen under Public Screens.

docs.title: Setting up a display
docs.text:
1. Connect the display computer to the venue network.
  2. Open the TMS address in a browser. See Connecting a device.
  3. From the home screen choose Scoreboard or Timer.
  4. Put the browser in full screen. In most browsers that is F11.

Tip

Turn off sleep, screen savers and automatic updates on display computers for the day.

docs.title: The Scoreboard
docs.text:
The scoreboard lists teams in rank order with their best score and their score in each round. It updates by itself as scoresheets come in.

Two tick boxes at the top add schedule panels:

Option Adds Match Schedule The upcoming matches, with the team on each table Judging Schedule The upcoming judging sessions, with the team in each pod

A common arrangement is one scoreboard with the match schedule in the competition area, and one with the judging schedule near the pits.

When there are more teams than fit on the screen the list scrolls by itself.

How ranks are worked out is explained in Rankings and the scoreboard.

docs.title: The Timer
docs.text:
The timer shows the match clock in large digits. It follows the head referee: it counts down when a match is started, and resets when the match ends.

The corner of the screen shows the match that is loaded, or the next match on the schedule and its start time.

docs.title: Sound
docs.text:
The Timer screen plays the match sounds:

  • a sound at the start of the match,
  • a sound when the end-game period begins,
  • a sound at the end of the match,
  • a short beep for each second of a countdown start, and
  • a stop sound if the head referee aborts the match.

Connect one computer showing the Timer to the venue sound system.

The head referee's Match Controller, the emcee's Match Announcer and the administrator's Dashboard play the same sounds. If any of those devices can be heard in the room as well, the audience hears each sound more than once, slightly out of step. Mute every device except the one connected to the speakers.

Browsers block sound until you interact with the page

After opening the Timer, click or tap somewhere on the page once. Otherwise the browser may stay silent for the first match. For a computer that plays sound all day, also allow sound permanently for the site; see Match timer. Test the sound with the head referee before the event starts.

docs.title: Assigning a timer to tables
docs.text:
On a wide screen the timer has an Assign Timer to Table/s button in the top right corner.

Select the tables this screen faces and confirm. The timer then shows the teams playing on those tables for the loaded match, underneath the clock. Use it when each pair of tables has its own screen.

The choice is remembered on that computer.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Each display is on the venue network and showing the right screen in full screen.
  • One timer computer is connected to the sound system, and other sound-playing devices are muted.
  • You have clicked on the timer page and heard a test start through the speakers.
  • Timers that face specific tables have those tables assigned.
  • Sleep and screen savers are off.

docs.title: Common situations
docs.text:
The scoreboard is empty

No schedule has been imported, or the display is not connected. Look for connection markers in the top bar.

The timer does not move when the match starts

The display has lost its live connection. Reload the page. If the top bar shows connection markers, see Troubleshooting.

There is no sound

Click on the timer page, check the computer's volume and output device, and check the browser tab is not muted.

Every sound plays twice

Another device with a sound-playing screen (Timer, Match Controller, Match Announcer or Dashboard) is audible. Mute it.

docs.title: I am an emcee
docs.text:
You keep the audience informed and the energy up. TMS gives you one screen with everything you need to announce a match, and lets you start the match timer yourself if your event works that way.

Your screen

Match Announcer.

docs.title: The Match Announcer screen
docs.text:
The screen follows the head referee. When they load a match, it appears for you.

  • The header shows the match that is loaded, or the next match on the schedule and how long until it is due.
  • The line-up shows each table in the match with the team's number, name and affiliation (their school or organisation), ready to read out.
  • The timer shows the match clock.
  • The Start and Countdown buttons start the match.

If nothing is loaded the screen says No Matches Loaded. If a match is loaded but the head referee has not marked it ready, the buttons show Not Ready.

docs.title: Announcing a match
docs.text:
1. Wait for the head referee to load the match. The line-up appears.
  2. Introduce the teams, table by table.
  3. Wait for the match to be marked ready. The start buttons become active.
  4. Start the match, if that is your job at this event.

docs.title: Starting the match
docs.text:
Button What happens Countdown A short countdown runs on every timer, with a beep each second, then the match starts with the start sound. Use this for a "3, 2, 1, LEGO!" start. Start The match starts immediately with the start sound.

Agree with the head referee before the event who presses the button. Either of you can start a match; only the head referee can stop one.

What the audience hears

A sound plays at the start, another when the end-game period begins, and another at the end. They normally reach the room from a Timer screen connected to the speakers. Your Match Announcer screen plays them too, so keep your device muted unless the screen and AV operator has asked to use it as the sound source.

docs.title: During the match
docs.text:
The clock on your screen is the same clock everyone sees. Call the end-game and the final seconds from it.

When the timer reaches zero the match is complete and your screen clears, ready for the next one.

docs.title: Common situations
docs.text:
The buttons say Not Ready

The head referee has not readied the match yet. Usually a table is still being reset or a team has not arrived.

The line-up is wrong

The schedule was changed after you last looked. Your screen is live, so read what it shows now.

I pressed Start too early

Tell the head referee. They can abort the timer and the match can be started again.

docs.title: I am an event administrator
docs.text:
You install and run the TMS server, prepare the event, create accounts and keep things healthy during the day. The admin account can open every screen and do everything any other role can.

Your screens

Setup, Dashboard, Users and Backups, plus every screen used by the other roles.

docs.title: Before the event
docs.text:
Follow the quick start. In short:

  1. Install and start the server.
  2. Log in as admin and change the admin password.
  3. Import the schedule.
  4. Choose the season.
  5. Create accounts for your volunteers.
  6. Check the Dashboard for integrity messages.

It is worth doing all of this the day before, on the network you will use at the venue. See Network planning.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Setup is where the event is configured. Each row has its own send button, and every setting can be changed while the event is running.

Section Setting Notes System Setup Event name Shown to identify the event System Setup Admin password Change this from the default System Setup Backup interval Minutes between automatic backups, 10 by default System Setup Backups to retain How many automatic backups are kept, 5 by default Schedule Setup Upload schedule The CSV file from the scheduler Season Setup Select Blueprint The season scoresheet, or Agnostic for score-only entry Game Scoring Setup Timer length Match length in seconds, 150 by default Game Scoring Setup Endgame length Seconds before the end at which the end-game sound plays, 30 by default Purge PURGE Deletes all event data, after a confirmation

Full details are in Event setup.

Purge

Purge empties the whole database, including user accounts and settings, and returns the server to a fresh install. It is intended for clearing a test event before the real one. Create a backup first.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The Dashboard is your live overview of the event.

  • Progress rings show completed matches, completed judging sessions and scoresheets received, each against the total expected.
  • Judging and Games rows show how far the event is running ahead of or behind the schedule.
  • Current Match shows the loaded match and the timer.
  • Integrity Messages lists problems the server has found in the event data.
  • Scores lists scoresheets as they arrive, by match, round, team and table.

docs.title: Reading integrity messages
docs.text:
Messages are either errors, which are mistakes that affect results, or warnings, which are worth a look. Each has a code such as E003 or W005. The most common ones on the day are:

Code Meaning Usual fix E003 A team has conflicting scores Two scoresheets exist for the same team and round. The judge advisor deletes or corrects one. W005 Match is complete but score not submitted A referee has not submitted yet. Follow up at the table. W006 Match is not complete but score submitted A score was submitted for a match that never ran on the timer. Mark the match complete or check the round.

The full list is in Integrity checks.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: Open Users from the side menu to add accounts, change passwords and set roles. Add default users creates one shared account per common role. See Users and passwords.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
The server backs itself up automatically. From Backups you can also create a backup on demand, download one, or restore one.

Warning

Restoring a backup replaces the current state of the event with the backup. Anything entered since that backup was taken is lost.

See Backups and restore.

docs.title: During the event
docs.text:
• Keep the server computer awake and plugged in.
  • Glance at the Dashboard between rounds.
  • Take a manual backup before any large change, such as re-importing a schedule.
  • Know where the troubleshooting page is.

docs.title: After the event
docs.text:
1. Ask the judge advisor to export the results from Team Data.
  2. Create a final backup and download it.
  3. Stop the server and keep the server folder.

docs.title: I am a head referee
docs.text:
You run the robot game: you decide which match is on, start the timer, and keep the match schedule and tables correct. A head referee account can also do everything a referee and a queuer can.

Your screens

Match Controller, Matches, Tables, Match Announcer, Referee Scoring and Queueing.

docs.title: The Match Controller
docs.text:
The Match Controller is one screen split in two.

  • On the right is the match schedule in order. Each row shows the match number, start time, and the team on each table.
  • On the left are the staged match, the schedule clock, the match timer and the controls.

docs.title: Running a match
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Staged: Stage a match from the list
    Staged --> Loaded: Load Match
    Loaded --> Staged: Unload Match
    Loaded --> Ready: Ready Match
    Ready --> Loaded: Unready Match
    Ready --> Running: Start or Countdown
    Running --> Complete: Timer reaches zero
    Running --> Ready: Abort
    Complete --> [*]
  1. Stage the match. Open a match row with the arrow on its right and select the blue stage button. The match and its tables appear on the left.
  2. Load Match. The match is now live for everyone: referees see their team, the emcee sees the line-up, and the timer screens show the match.
  3. Check the table status next to each table (see below).
  4. Ready Match when the tables are set and teams are in place. This unlocks the timer buttons.
  5. Start begins the match immediately. Countdown plays a short countdown first, then starts.
  6. When the timer reaches zero the match is marked complete. Stage the next one.

Use Abort to stop a running timer, for example after a false start. The match is not marked complete, so you can start it again.

docs.title: Table status
docs.text:
Each table in the loaded match shows a status that comes from the referee's tablet.

Status Colour Meaning SIG Red No tablet is scoring on this table. Nobody has Referee Scoring open with this table selected. STBY Amber A tablet is on this table but is not showing this match's team yet, usually because the previous scoresheet has not been submitted. RDY Green A tablet is on this table and is showing the right team.

You can ready and start a match whatever the statuses say. They are there to tell you whether the referees are with you.

docs.title: Single and Multi
docs.text:
The switch above the schedule chooses how many matches you stage at once.

  • Single stages one match.
  • Multi lets you stage several matches and run them together on one timer. Use this when the schedule runs matches on different tables at the same time.

docs.title: The schedule clock
docs.text: The red or green clock above the timer shows how far the event is from the next scheduled match start. Negative and red means you are running behind schedule.

docs.title: Fixing a match on the spot
docs.text:
Open a match row to reveal four buttons.

Button What it does Stage (blue) Stages the match for loading Reschedule (purple) Moves one team from this match to another match and table Edit (orange) Opens the match editor Delete (red) Deletes the match

To reschedule a team, choose the team, then the match to move it to, then the table it will play on, and confirm.

docs.title: Matches
docs.text:
The Matches page lists every match with its integrity status, start time and tables. Use it for changes that are easier with the whole schedule in view.

  • Add match creates a new match.
  • The pencil on a row opens the match editor, where you can change the match number and start time, mark it completed, and add, change or remove the teams on each table.
  • The bin on a row deletes the match.

The banner at the top shows how many matches are complete and how many match and team issues the integrity checks have found. A row with a warning or error icon has a problem; see Integrity checks.

Replaying a match

If a match must be replayed, open the match editor, clear Completed, and run it again from the Match Controller. Ask the judge advisor to remove the scoresheets from the first attempt.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text: The Tables page lists the robot game tables. You can add a table, rename one, or delete one. Table names must match the names used in the matches.

docs.title: Starting the timer from the announcer screen
docs.text: The Match Announcer screen has the same Start and Countdown buttons. If your emcee starts matches, you only need to load and ready them. See the Emcee guide.

docs.title: Common situations
docs.text:
A referee's table shows SIG

Their tablet is not on Referee Scoring, has no table selected, or has lost its connection. Ask them to open Referee Scoring and select their table.

A team is at the wrong table

Either move the team in the match editor, or ask the referees to swap tablets' selected tables. The scoresheet is recorded against the table the referee has selected.

I loaded the wrong match

Select Unload Match, then stage and load the correct one. Nothing is recorded until the timer finishes.

The timer was started by mistake

Select Abort. The match stays ready and is not marked complete.

docs.title: I am a judge advisor
docs.text:
You look after the teams and everything recorded against them: their details, their judging sessions, and their robot game scores. You are also the person who corrects scoresheets when something was entered wrongly. A judge advisor account can do everything a judge account can.

Your screens

Teams, Team Data, Judging Sessions and Pods.

docs.title: Teams
docs.text:
The Teams page is where you look at one team in detail.

Select a team from the list. The page shows:

  • the team's rank, and how many of its matches and judging sessions are complete,
  • any team issues found by the integrity checks,
  • the team's details: number, name and affiliation, which you can edit and save with Update Team, and
  • the team's scoresheets, one row per submission, with round, score, table, referee and timestamp.

Use Add Team to add a team that was not in the schedule file, and Delete Team to remove one.

Warning

Deleting a team also deletes its scoresheets. It does not remove the team from matches or judging sessions it was scheduled in; the integrity checks will flag those until the head referee and you update the schedule.

docs.title: Correcting a scoresheet
docs.text:
Referees cannot change a scoresheet after submitting it. You can.

On the team's page, each scoresheet row can be edited or deleted.

  • Edit Score opens the sheet. You can change the round, table, referee and match number, change the answers, or mark it as a no-show. The score is recalculated from the answers when you save.
  • Delete Score removes the sheet entirely.
  • Add Score Sheet creates a sheet for the team by hand, for example from a paper scoresheet.

Resolving conflicting scores

The error E003, Team has conflicting scores, means a team has two scoresheets for the same round. Decide which is correct, then delete the other or change its round.

A sheet you have changed is marked as modified along with your username, so there is a record of who corrected it.

docs.title: Team Data
docs.text:
Team Data is a table of every team with its rank and, for each round, its score, Gracious Professionalism rating and the referee's private comment.

  • Columns chooses which columns are shown.
  • The filter boxes under the column headers narrow the table.
  • Export downloads the table as a CSV file, exactly as it is currently filtered and with the columns currently shown.

Use the export for your results and for anything you need to pass to the judges, such as Gracious Professionalism ratings and comments.

docs.title: Judging Sessions
docs.text:
The Judging Sessions page lists every session with its number, start and end times, and the team in each pod.

  • Add Session creates a session.
  • The pencil on a row opens the session editor, where you can change the number and times and add, change or remove the team in each pod.
  • The bin on a row deletes the session.

docs.title: Tracking judging progress
docs.text:
For each team in a session you can tick off three items as their rubrics come in:

  • Core Values
  • Innovation
  • Robot Design

A pod is shown as done when all three are ticked. The banner at the top of the page shows how many sessions are complete, and the Dashboard shows the same count to the event administrator.

Note

TMS tracks that judging rubrics have been received. It does not record the rubric scores themselves.

docs.title: Pods
docs.text: The Pods page lists the judging rooms. You can add, rename or remove a pod. Pod names must match the names used in the sessions.

docs.title: Integrity messages for judging
docs.text:
The session list shows an icon on any session with a problem. Common ones:

Code Meaning E010 Team has more than one judging session E011 Team is not in any judging sessions E013 Team has a match overlapping with its judging session W009 Team has a judging session within 10 minutes of a match

The full list is in Integrity checks.

docs.title: End of the day
docs.text:
1. Check that no team has an error on the Teams page.
  2. Open Team Data, choose the columns you need and Export.
  3. Tell the event administrator you are done, so they can take the final backup.

docs.title: I am a judge
docs.text:
TMS is mainly a robot game system. Judging rubrics are completed outside TMS, so a judge account has very little to do in it.

Your screens

The public Scoreboard and Timer. A judge account does not currently unlock any further screens.

docs.title: What you can see
docs.text:
Anyone, logged in or not, can open the Scoreboard from the home screen. It shows:

  • every team's rank and scores by round, and
  • with the Judging Schedule box ticked, the upcoming judging sessions with the team in each pod.

That second view is the useful one for a judging room: it tells you who is due next and where.

docs.title: What you need from the judge advisor
docs.text:
The judge advisor is the judging contact in TMS. They:

  • keep the judging sessions and pods up to date if the schedule changes,
  • tick off each team's Core Values, Innovation and Robot Design rubrics as they are handed in, and
  • can give you each team's Gracious Professionalism ratings and referee comments from the robot game, exported from Team Data.

If your session list looks wrong, or a team has not arrived, tell the judge advisor.

Need more access?

If a judge needs to edit sessions or see team data, the event administrator can give their account the judge advisor role instead.

docs.title: I am a queuer
docs.text:
You make sure the right teams are at the right tables at the right time. TMS shows you what is coming up and lets you record which teams have arrived, so the head referee knows when a match can start.

Your screen

Queueing. It is designed to work on a phone as well as a tablet.

docs.title: The queueing screen
docs.text:
The screen is a list of matches in schedule order. Each match is a card showing:

  • the match number and start time, and
  • each table in the match with the team due on it.

Cards change appearance as the day moves on:

  • the match that the head referee has loaded is highlighted, because those are the teams you need at the tables now, and
  • completed matches are shown as done.

docs.title: Checking a team in
docs.text:
Tap a team on a match card to change its check-in status. Each tap moves it to the next state.

Status Colour Meaning Not checked in None The team has not arrived at the table Checked in Green The team is at the table and ready Not playing Orange The team will not play this match

When a match is loaded and a team in it is still not checked in, the card draws your attention to it. Those are the teams to go and find.

Tip

Mark a team as not playing as soon as you know they will not make it. It tells the head referee not to wait, and the referee at that table can record a no-show.

docs.title: A good rhythm
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Look two matches ahead] --> B[Find those teams in the pits]
    B --> C[Walk them to the queue]
    C --> D[Check them in at the table]
    D --> A
  1. Work ahead of the loaded match. By the time a match is loaded its teams should already be queued.
  2. Check teams in as they reach their table, not when you find them in the pits.
  3. If a team cannot be found, tell the head referee early. They can reschedule the team to a later match.

docs.title: Common situations
docs.text:
The schedule on my screen changed

The head referee has edited a match. Your screen always shows the live schedule, so follow what it shows now.

A team says they are on a different table

Trust the screen. If the team has been told otherwise by the head referee, the head referee needs to update the match so the referees see the same thing.

I tapped the wrong team

Tap it again until it shows the right status.

docs.title: I am a referee
docs.text:
You score matches at your table on a tablet. TMS shows you the right team, works out the score as you answer, checks the sheet for mistakes and sends it in.

Your screen

Referee Scoring.

docs.title: Getting ready
docs.text:
1. Open TMS on your tablet and log in with the referee account you were given.
  2. From the home screen open Referee Scoring.
  3. In the header, select your table.
  4. Enter your name as the referee.

That is all the setup there is. Leave Referee Scoring open: while it is open with a table selected, the head referee can see that your table is staffed.

docs.title: The scoring screen
docs.text:
The header across the top shows:

  • your table,
  • the team you are about to score,
  • the match number and how many matches there are, and
  • the round.

The team, match and round fill in by themselves from the schedule once the head referee loads a match. You do not choose them.

Below the header is the scoresheet, one block per mission. At the bottom are the running score and three buttons: No Show, Clear and Submit.

docs.title: Scoring a match
docs.text:
1. Wait for the match to finish.
  2. Go through the scoresheet with the team, answering each question.
    • Yes/No and multiple choice questions are buttons. Select the answer.
    • Questions with a large number range show a counter. Use +1 and −1, or +5 and −5, to reach the number.
  3. Watch the score in the bottom corner update as you go.
  4. Set Gracious Professionalism. It defaults to 3 - Accomplished.
  5. Add a private comment if you need to. This is only seen by event staff.
  6. Select Submit and confirm.

After you submit, the sheet resets and the tablet waits for your next team.

Tip

After you answer a question the page moves on to the next one for you. Counter questions stay where they are so you can keep tapping.

docs.title: When the sheet will not submit
docs.text:
The scoresheet checks itself. If an answer is impossible, a message appears in red under the question and Submit is blocked until it is fixed.

Examples:

  • a bonus is claimed without the thing it depends on,
  • more items are counted in a scoring area than exist on the field, or
  • a question has no answer.

Fix the highlighted answer and submit again. The message tells you which rule was broken.

A comment is required for some GP ratings

If Gracious Professionalism is anything other than 3 - Accomplished, you must enter a private comment explaining why before you can submit.

docs.title: A team did not turn up
docs.text: Select No Show and confirm. This records the round for that team with a score of zero and marks it as a no-show, so the event does not show the score as missing.

docs.title: Starting again
docs.text: Clear resets every answer to its default. Use it if you started scoring the wrong team's run. It cannot be undone.

docs.title: If you make a mistake after submitting
docs.text:
You cannot change a scoresheet once it is submitted. Tell the head referee or judge advisor straight away, with the team number and round. The judge advisor can correct or delete the sheet.

Do not submit a second sheet for the same team and round to "fix" the first. That creates a conflict that someone then has to resolve.

docs.title: Common situations
docs.text:
My tablet shows the wrong team

Check the table in the header is yours. If it is, the previous sheet may not have been submitted, or the head referee has not loaded the next match yet.

No team is showing

No match is loaded for your table. Wait for the head referee.

There are connection markers in the top bar

Your tablet has lost the server. See Connecting a device. Keep the tablet on the scoring screen; your answers stay on the screen and you can submit when it reconnects.

The scoresheet is just a score box

The event is running in Agnostic mode, where you enter the final score yourself instead of answering questions. See Scoring and scoresheets.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Does TMS need the internet?

No. Everything runs on the local network. Internet is only needed to download TMS, or for optional remote access.

What devices can be used?

Anything with a modern web browser, plus the iOS app. Tablets are ideal for referees; phones work for queuers; laptops suit the head referee, judge advisor and admin. Some management screens need a larger screen and will say so on a phone.

How many devices can connect?

There is no fixed limit. A typical event with a tablet per table, a few laptops and several display screens is well within what a modest laptop can serve.

Which seasons are supported?

See Seasons and games. Any other game can be run in Agnostic mode with manual score entry.

Does TMS handle judging scores?

No. TMS schedules judging sessions and tracks whether each team's rubrics have been received, but the rubric scores are recorded outside TMS.

Can I try it before an event?

Yes. Run the server on your own computer, open http://localhost:8080, log in as admin and import a schedule. When you are finished, Purge in Setup clears it, or just delete the folder.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Where do I get a schedule file?

From the FLL scheduler used by FIRST Australia. See Schedules.

Can I run an event without a schedule file?

Yes. Add teams, tables, matches, pods and sessions by hand on their pages. It is slower, but everything the import creates can be created manually.

Can I change the schedule during the event?

Yes, at any time. Changes appear on every device immediately. See Editing after import.

Can two events run at once?

Yes, with two servers. Use two folders and two ports, for example --port 8080 and --port 8081. Each server is one event.

Can I move an event to another computer?

Yes, with a backup. See Moving an event to another computer.

docs.title: On the day
docs.text:
A tablet's battery died mid-scoresheet. Is anything lost?

Only the answers on that screen that had not been submitted. Charge or swap the tablet, log in, select the table and score again.

The server computer restarted. Is the event lost?

No. Everything is saved as it happens. Start the server again from the same folder and devices reconnect by themselves.

Can a referee change a score after submitting?

No. The judge advisor can. This is deliberate, so that every correction goes through one person.

Can two referees score the same table?

Only one scoresheet should be submitted per team per round. If two are submitted, TMS flags a conflict and the judge advisor resolves it.

How are ties broken?

By second-best score, then third-best, and so on. See Rankings and the scoreboard.

Can the scoreboard be hidden for the final round?

There is no setting for it. Take the scoreboard off the public screens, or show the Timer instead.

Why do I hear the match sounds more than once?

Several screens play them: the Timer, the Match Controller, the Match Announcer and the Dashboard. Connect one to the speakers and mute the rest. See Match timer.

docs.title: Data and privacy
docs.text:
Where is the data stored?

Only on the server computer, in the server folder. Nothing is sent anywhere else unless you turn on remote access.

What personal data does TMS hold?

Team names and affiliations, the names referees type in, usernames and passwords for the event, and referees' private comments. Treat backups accordingly.

How do I delete an event's data?

Delete the server folder, including its backups folder, and any backups you downloaded.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Is this version still developed?

This is the legacy codebase. It receives season updates and maintenance. New features are going into the rebuild; see the repository.

How do I report a bug or a scoring error?

Open an issue. For a scoring error include the season, the mission and the rule reference. For anything else, see what to send with a bug report.

docs.title: Logs and files
docs.text: When something goes wrong, the server's logs and the layout of its folder tell you most of what you need.

docs.title: The server folder
docs.text:
tms/
├── tms_server          the server program (tms_server.exe on Windows)
├── tms_client/         the web client served at /ui
├── log_config/         logging settings
├── tms.kvdb/           the event database
├── backups/            backup .zip files
├── logs/
│   ├── tms.log         server activity
│   └── db.log          database and live-data activity
├── cert.pem            TLS certificate, when used
└── key.rsa             TLS private key, when used

docs.title: Log files
docs.text:
File Contains logs/tms.log Logins, scoresheet submissions, calculated scores, match and timer events, integrity messages, errors logs/db.log Device connections and disconnections, subscriptions to live data, data changes

Each file grows to 10 MB, then is renamed to tms.1.log (or db.1.log) and a new file is started. Up to ten old files are kept.

The same messages are printed in the server's terminal window as they happen.

docs.title: Reading a log line
docs.text:
[2026-10-10 18:13:49 WARN tms_server::database::extensions::game_score_sheet_extensions LINE: 68] Calculated score for: Table 1, 530
Part Meaning 2026-10-10 18:13:49 When it happened, in the server computer's local time WARN The level: INFO, WARN or ERROR tms_server::... Which part of the server wrote it LINE: 68 The line in the source code The rest The message

Not every WARN or ERROR is a problem

Some routine events are logged at a higher level so that they stand out. A scoresheet rejected by validation, or an integrity message such as [E003], appears as an ERROR line. That is the system working as intended.

docs.title: Useful things to search for
docs.text: Search for To find Calculated score for Every scoresheet the server accepted, with table and score Failed to submit GameScoreSheet Scoresheets the server rejected, and why Login attempt failed Wrong passwords connected / disconnected Devices joining and leaving Hosting on The address the server started on Tunnel active Remote access coming up

docs.title: Changing how much is logged
docs.text:
The files in log_config control what is written. Release builds use release_log4rs.yaml.

log_config/release_log4rs.yaml (extract)
root:
  level: info # (1)!
  appenders:
    - tms_server_stdout
    - tms_server
  1. Change to debug for much more detail, or warn for less. The server re-reads this file every 30 seconds, so you do not need to restart it.

Use debug only while investigating a problem. It records every message between the server and each device.

docs.title: The database
docs.text:
tms.kvdb is a folder, not a single file. Treat it as a unit:

  • Do not open, edit, move or delete anything inside it while the server is running.
  • Do not copy it as a way of taking a backup. Use the Backups page, which produces a consistent snapshot.

docs.title: On the client
docs.text:
The connection page (cog icon) shows the client's version and build number. Include both when reporting a problem.

In a web browser, the developer console (usually F12) shows errors from the client. A screenshot of anything red there is useful in a bug report.

docs.title: What to send with a bug report
docs.text:
• TMS version and build
  • The platform the server runs on (Windows, Linux, macOS or Docker)
  • What you were doing and what you expected
  • logs/tms.log and logs/db.log covering the time of the problem
  • A backup of the event, if the problem can be reproduced from it and it contains nothing confidential

Report issues at github.com/CJBuchel/TMS/issues.

Check before you share

A backup contains team names, usernames and passwords for that event. Share it only with someone you trust, and never post it publicly.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the symptom you can see. If you are at an event right now, the first two sections cover most problems.

docs.title: First checks
docs.text:
Before anything else:

  1. Is the server window still open on the server computer, and has that computer gone to sleep?
  2. Is the device on the same network as the server?
  3. Has the server's address changed since the morning?
  4. Does reloading the page fix it?

docs.title: The device will not connect
docs.text:
The top bar shows connection markers such as [DC|DC|DC] and they do not clear.

flowchart TD
    A[Markers stay in the top bar] --> B{What do they show?}
    B -- "DC first" --> C[The server cannot be reached]
    B -- "OK first, DC after" --> D[The server is reachable but live updates are not]
    C --> E{Can another device open the server address?}
    E -- No --> F[Server problem: is it running, awake and on the network?]
    E -- Yes --> G[This device: wrong network or wrong address]
    D --> H[Reload the page, then check for a proxy or filter blocking WebSockets]
[DC|DC|DC] on one device

That device cannot reach the server.

  • Check it is on the event Wi-Fi and not a guest or mobile network.
  • Open the connection page (cog icon) and check the Server IP Address and Server Port. Enter the right ones and select Connect.
  • In a browser, make sure the address begins with http:// unless the server was started with --tls.
[DC|DC|DC] on every device

The server is not reachable by anyone.

  • Look at the server computer. Is tms_server still running? If the window has closed, start it again; no data is lost.
  • Has the computer gone to sleep, or disconnected from the network?
  • Has its IP address changed? The server prints its address when it starts. See Give the server a fixed address.
  • Is a firewall blocking the port? See Firewalls.
[OK|DC|DC] or [OK|OK|DC]

The server answers, but the live connection does not stay up.

  • Reload the page.
  • Some school and corporate networks block WebSocket connections. Try the device on your own router.
  • If the server was restarted, devices reconnect by themselves within a few seconds.
It works on the server computer but not on other devices

This is nearly always the firewall on the server computer, or client isolation on the Wi-Fi. See Network planning.

The browser warns that the connection is not private

The server is running with --tls and a self-signed certificate. Choose to continue. See Self-signed certificates.

docs.title: Logging in
docs.text:
Incorrect Username or Password

Usernames and passwords are case sensitive. The default accounts use the username as the password. An admin can reset a password on the Users page.

I have forgotten the admin password

There is no reset from the login page. Options:

  • If another admin account exists, log in with it and set the password in Setup.
  • Otherwise, restore a backup taken before the password was changed. See Backups and restore.
A screen I need is not on my home screen

Your account does not have the role for it. See Roles at a glance and ask an admin to update your account. Log out and in again afterwards.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Submit is blocked with a red message under a question

The scoresheet has an answer that breaks a rule of the game. Read the message and fix that answer. See When the sheet will not submit.

Comment Required

Gracious Professionalism is set to something other than 3 - Accomplished. Enter a private comment and submit again.

No team or the wrong team on the scoring screen
  • Check the table selected in the header.
  • If no match is loaded, there is no team to show. Wait for the head referee.
  • If the previous scoresheet has not been submitted, submit or clear it.
A scoresheet was rejected by the server

The server runs the same checks as the tablet. A rejection means the answers are invalid or the team number is not in the event. The message says which. If the team is missing, the judge advisor adds it on the Teams page.

A score is wrong after it was submitted

The judge advisor corrects or deletes it on the team's page. See Correcting a scoresheet.

The scoreboard shows Conflict

A team has two scoresheets for one round. See Conflicting scores.

The scoresheet shows the wrong season

An admin sets the season in Setup → Season Setup. See Seasons and games.

docs.title: Matches and the timer
docs.text:
Start and Countdown are greyed out

A match must be loaded and ready first. See Running a match.

A table shows SIG or STBY

See Table status. SIG means no tablet is scoring on that table; STBY means the tablet has not caught up to this match.

The timer was started by mistake

The head referee selects Abort. The match is not marked complete.

There is no sound

Browsers block sound until someone has interacted with the page. On the device that should be heard, click on the page once, then check the volume, the output device and that the tab is not muted. See Where the timer appears.

The sounds play twice

Two devices with a sound-playing screen (Timer, Match Controller, Match Announcer or Dashboard) are both audible. Mute all but one.

A match will not show as complete

A match is completed by the timer running to zero. If it was played without the timer, the head referee can tick Completed in the match editor.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
The schedule will not import

See If the import fails.

There are integrity messages after importing

The schedule itself has a problem, such as a team with no judging session. Look up the code in Integrity checks.

docs.title: The server
docs.text:
The server closes immediately when started
  • Start it from its own folder. It needs the log_config and tms_client folders beside it.
  • Check another program is not already using the port. Try --port 8081.
  • Run it from a terminal so that you can read the message it prints.
The server stopped during a restore

The backup file could not be loaded. Start the server again and restore a different backup.

The web page is blank

docs.text:
Collect the following and open an issue:

  • the TMS version, from the connection page,
  • what you did and what happened, and
  • the log files from the time of the problem. See Logs and files.
